Slice: Register Neighbor

Intent

Let a neighbor join the tool shed by signing themselves up, so they can borrow tools. Signing up records the neighbor's name and the email address the shed uses to reach them. A new neighbor is active and can borrow straight away.

Trigger & Actor

A person who wants to join, from the Sign Up screen. They sign themselves up; the shed manager doesn't enroll neighbors. Someone whose earlier account is closed may sign up again here, as a new account. How a person is recognised once signed up is the open identity question below.

Command / Input

Command: Register Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID. Text fields have leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed; text that is empty after that counts as absent.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new account, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different account already registered (INV-REG-7).
name Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3). Need not be unique (INV-REG-9).
email Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3). Must not be held by another account under INV-REG-4. Format and comparison rules are open questions below.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Sign Up @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Registered → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors and My Account (their own slices, right after this one); and, for the neighbor's name and email, Tool Inventory (name only), Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command. Identifies the account everywhere from here on.
name Text yes From the command, trimmed.
email Text yes From the command, trimmed. The account's email until a later Neighbor Email Changed replaces it.
registeredAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the sign-up date.

The event records a fact that never changes. A later email change is its own event; the name is never changed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Registered starts the new account's entry in two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • Neighbors (slices/neighbors.md) lists the new neighbor to the shed manager as active.
  • My Account (slices/my-account.md) shows the new neighbor their account.

Both are eventually consistent: the new account appears once each view has caught up with Neighbor Registered.

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor signs themselves up; the shed manager does not enroll neighbors. Every account starts active: Neighbor Registered is the only event that starts an account, and suspension and closure come later, from other slices. The Neighbors view shows a new account as active (INV-NBRS-2), and Check Out Tool lends to it under its usual rules.

  • INV-REG-3: Sign-up requires a name and an email address.
    • The shed emails neighbors, and only by email: overdue notices to borrowers and pickup notices to holders both go to this address.
    • A name or email that is empty, or only whitespace, is missing.
  • INV-REG-4: A sign-up is refused if its email belongs to an account that is not closed, or to a closed account that was suspended when it was closed.
    • An account's email is its current one: the email it registered with, or the latest Neighbor Email Changed for it. An email an account has changed away from belongs to no one.
    • One account per email. A closed account's email can be used again, so a neighbor who left can come back with the same address.
    • An account closed while suspended keeps its email for good, so a suspended neighbor can't get around the suspension by closing their account and signing up again with the same email. A suspended neighbor can't change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email), so that email is the one they were suspended under.
    • A sign-up with a different email is accepted, even from someone whose earlier account was closed while suspended. Email is the only thing that identifies a neighbor. The shed manager sees both accounts on the Neighbors screen and can suspend the new one.
    • The same rule applies when a neighbor changes their email (INV-CEM-2, Change Email).
  • INV-REG-5: Signing up has no approval or verification step.
    • Neighbor Registered is recorded straight from the request. Nothing waits for the shed manager, and the email address isn't confirmed first. The new neighbor can borrow straight away, under Check Out Tool's usual rules.
  • INV-REG-6: A neighbor whose account is closed may sign up again, and doing so creates a new account.
    • The new account has its own neighbor ID. The closed account stays closed; it is never reopened.
  • INV-REG-7: Registering with a neighbor ID that is already used adds nothing new.
    • A repeat with the same name and email, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the account since. A repeat with different details is refused (neighbor-id-in-use).
  • INV-REG-8: Each account gets its own neighbor ID when it registers, and keeps it for good.
    • The neighbor ID is how every later event, view and command refers to the account. Names and emails are for people to read and for the shed to send email to.
  • INV-REG-9: Neighbor names need not be unique.
    • Two neighbors may both be called "Sam Lee". Accounts are told apart by neighbor ID, and only the email is checked for uniqueness.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-5, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: no account uses the email address ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up from the Sign Up screen as neighbor N1, with the name "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and the time it was recorded. Nothing waits for approval or email confirmation.
  • Whitespace is removed (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up with the name " Ana Ruiz " and the email " ana@example.org "
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org.
  • No name (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up with ana@example.org and a name that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with name-missing: "Please enter your name." No event is recorded.
  • No email (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up as "Ana Ruiz" with an email that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with email-missing: "Please enter your email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by an active account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N2 with ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by a suspended account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2 uses ben@example.org and is suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N3 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: Ana's account N1, using ana@example.org, was closed while active
    • When: Ana signs up as N4 with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N4, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N1 keeps its neighbor ID and stays closed.
  • Email of an account closed while suspended (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N5 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended, reinstated, then closed (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was suspended, then reinstated, and then closed while active
    • When: Ben signs up as N9 with ben@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N9. The account wasn't suspended when it was closed, so its email is free again.
  • Different email after closing while suspended (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: Ben signs up as N5 with ben.new@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N5, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N2 stays closed.
  • Email an account has changed away from (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 registered with ana@oldmail.example and has since changed its email to ana@example.org
    • When: someone signs up as N6 with ana@oldmail.example
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N6. No account holds ana@oldmail.example any more.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-REG-9)
    • Given: Sam Lee's account N7 uses sam@example.org
    • When: another person signs up as N8, also named "Sam Lee", with sam.lee@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N8. There are two accounts named "Sam Lee".
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • The same request after the account was closed (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and N1 has since been closed
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. N1 stays closed.
  • A neighbor ID reused for different details (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: a Register Neighbor request arrives for N1 with "Ben Cole" and ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with neighbor-id-in-use: "That neighbor ID is already used by another account." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the person on the Sign Up screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

Reason Sentence Rule
name-missing Please enter your name. INV-REG-3
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-REG-3
email-in-use That email address is already used by an account. INV-REG-4
neighbor-id-in-use That neighbor ID is already used by another account. INV-REG-7

email-in-use is the same for every case in INV-REG-4, so a refused sign-up never reveals whether the other account is active, suspended, or closed while suspended.

neighbor-id-in-use can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same neighbor ID and the same name and email, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, even if the account has since been suspended, closed, or had its email changed. So a retry after a lost response never creates a second account. The repeat is recognised by its neighbor ID, and is checked before the email rule, so it is never refused as email-in-use by its own earlier registration.

Two sign-ups with the same email at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Registered happen as one step, so at most one is recorded. The other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. No email is sent on sign-up.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: anyone may sign up; signing up needs no existing account. How a neighbor is recognised afterwards, so that later actions are theirs, is the open identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Registered holds the neighbor's name and email address. It is read by the shed manager's screens (Neighbors, Tool Inventory, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors, Suspended Neighbors), by the neighbor's own My Account, and by the two email to-do lists. Whether any neighbor-facing screen shows another neighbor's name is the open question in Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) about showing who has a tool. Whether a closed account's details are kept for good is an open question below.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply INV-REG-4 and INV-REG-7, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (this slice): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Those slices aren't yet written in depth. These names are this slice's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors and My Account (a new entry); Tool Inventory, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the neighbor's name and email). Every later neighbor action (check out, hold, extend, return, change email, close account) and every shed-manager action on a neighbor refers to the account by its neighbor ID.

Open Questions

  • How does anyone identify themselves to the system, the shed manager and neighbors alike? (brief 10 A1)
    • Signing up creates an account, but nothing in the model says how that person is recognised afterwards, so that a checkout or hold is theirs. The same question is open for the shed manager in Add Tool.
    • Options: (a) callers say who they are, and nothing checks it; (b) a sign-in outside the model supplies the neighbor's ID or the shed-manager role, with no new events; (c) sign-in and roles are modeled as events and slices.
    • Recommendation: (b). Neighbors need to be recognised before a loan can be theirs, and (b) adds nothing to the model.
  • What makes an email address acceptable at sign-up? (brief 11 B3)
    • Options: (a) only that it is present; (b) a basic shape check (one "@", with text on both sides and a dot in the part after it), refused as email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address."
    • Recommendation: (b). A mistyped address otherwise only shows up later as an undelivered notice.
  • Are two emails that differ only in capital letters the same address? (brief 11 B4)
    • For example, Ana@Example.org and ana@example.org.
    • Recommendation: yes for the one-account-per-email rule: compare without regard to case, and keep the address as typed. Otherwise one person can hold two accounts with the same mailbox.
  • Are there length limits on a neighbor's name and email? (brief 11 B5)
    • Recommendation: name up to 100 characters, email up to 254. A longer one is refused with the limit in the reason, never cut short. This matches the limits proposed for tool names.
  • Does the shed's existing baseline of keeping personal data with the loan and hold history, with no erasure, carry over to neighbors' names and emails? (brief 11 B7)
    • A closed account's email is needed to refuse a sign-up with the email of an account closed while suspended (INV-REG-4), and the closed account stays on the shed manager's Neighbors screen.
    • Recommendation: yes, it carries over: details are kept and never erased. If a neighbor must be able to have their details erased, that is a new event and slice.
  • What does a person see when they sign up with an email that can't be used? (brief 11 B6)
    • INV-REG-4 refuses three cases with one reason, email-in-use, and the sentence "That email address is already used by an account." For an email held by an account closed while suspended, that sentence isn't true: the account is closed.
    • Options: (a) one reason and one sentence for all three cases, reworded to be true in each: "That email address can't be used to sign up."; (b) a separate reason for the closed-while-suspended case, telling the person why.
    • Recommendation: (a). It keeps one reason, never reveals another account's status, and stops the sentence misleading.
  • Whether any neighbor-facing screen shows who has or holds a tool (brief 11 B1).
"},{"index":1,"name":"Change Email","x0":289.76,"x1":433.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Change Email

Intent

Let a neighbor change the email address the shed uses for them, from My Account, so a wrong or outdated address can be put right and overdue and pickup emails reach them. The new address takes effect at once, and the old one is free for anyone to use.

Trigger & Actor

A neighbor, from their own My Account screen, for their own account. My Account offers Change Email on any account that isn't closed (INV-MYAC-9); a suspended neighbor is offered it and refused with a reason they can see. The shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails.

Command / Input

Command: Change Email

A NeighborId is a UUID. Text has leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed; text that is empty after that counts as absent.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The account whose email changes, which must be the neighbor making the request (INV-CEM-1) and a registered account (INV-CEM-10).
email Text yes The new email. Trimmed; must not then be empty (INV-CEM-11). Must not be held by another account under INV-CEM-2. Format and comparison rules are the open questions shared with Register Neighbor, below.

There is no name field: only the email can be changed. A neighbor's name stays as they registered it.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Account @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Email Changed → context Neighbors Read by: My Account and Neighbors (the email shown); Overdue Loans To Notify and Pickup Notices To Send (the address the next email goes to); Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the email shown to the shed manager).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
email Text yes From the command, trimmed. The account's current email from now on.
changedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event never changes. A later change records a new Neighbor Email Changed. An account's current email is the email of its latest Neighbor Email Changed, or of its Neighbor Registered if it has never changed it.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Email Changed updates the email in My Account, Neighbors, Overdue Loans To Notify, Pickup Notices To Send, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors, each specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent: the new email shows once each has caught up. Every overdue or pickup email the shed sends from then on, including one for a loan or set-aside already waiting to be emailed, goes to the new address.

Invariants / Business Rules

Changing the email resends nothing. A notice already sent, or already recorded as undelivered, is not tried again at the new address: no further attempt is made after a failure (Record Overdue Notice Failure, INV-ONF-6).

  • INV-CEM-1: A neighbor changes their own email themselves, from My Account.
    • The request must come from the neighbor whose account it names. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question below. The shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails.
  • INV-CEM-2: The new email is refused if it belongs to an account that is not closed, or to a closed account that was suspended when it was closed.
    • This is the same one-account-per-email rule as at sign-up (INV-REG-4, Register Neighbor). An account's email is always its current one.
  • INV-CEM-3: A neighbor whose account is closed can't change their email.
    • After closing, My Account is read-only.
  • INV-CEM-3a: A suspended neighbor can't change their email. The change is refused with a reason they can see, and they can change it once reinstated.
    • Otherwise a suspended neighbor could change to a new address, close their account, and sign up again with their original address.
  • INV-CEM-4: Once changed, the account's email is the new one.
    • Every later check of INV-CEM-2 and INV-REG-4 treats the new email as held by this account.
  • INV-CEM-5: The old email is released.
    • No account holds it any more, so it can be used to sign up or by another neighbor's change.
  • INV-CEM-7: The new email takes effect at once, with no verification.
    • Neighbor Email Changed is recorded straight from the request; nothing is sent to the new address first.
  • INV-CEM-9: Asking to change the email to the one the account already has succeeds and records nothing.
    • The comparison is made after trimming. So a repeated request, after a lost response, never records a second change.
    • The command carries no "from" email. A late copy of an older request, arriving after a later change, counts as a new request and changes the email again.
  • INV-CEM-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-CEM-11: A new email is required.
    • An email that is empty, or only whitespace, is missing.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-CEM-1, INV-CEM-4, INV-CEM-7)
    • Given: Ana's account N1 is active with ana@oldmail.example, and no other account uses ana@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana@example.org from My Account
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with ana@example.org and the time it was recorded. Nothing is sent to the new address first.
  • Whitespace is removed (INV-CEM-11)
    • Given: N1 is active with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Ana changes her email to " ana@example.org "
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded with ana@example.org.
  • Same email as now (INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: N1's current email is ana@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana@example.org
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: Neighbor Email Changed was recorded for N1, to ana@example.org
    • When: the same Change Email request for N1, ana@example.org, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • No email (INV-CEM-11)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to an empty value, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with email-missing: "Please enter your email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by an active account (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Ben's active account N2 uses ben@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by a suspended account (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Cleo's account N3 uses cleo@example.org and is suspended
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to cleo@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Email of an account closed while suspended (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Dan's account N4, using dan@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to dan@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Email of an account closed while active (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Eve's account N5, using eve@example.org, was closed while active
    • When: Ana changes her email to eve@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with eve@example.org.
  • Old email released (INV-CEM-5)
    • Given: Ana changed N1's email from ana@oldmail.example to ana@example.org
    • When: Ben asks to change N2's email to ana@oldmail.example
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N2, with ana@oldmail.example.
  • The new email is held from then on (INV-CEM-4)
    • Given: Ana changed N1's email to ana@example.org
    • When: Ben asks to change N2's email to ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-CEM-3a)
    • Given: N1 is suspended, with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't change your email while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Changing the email after reinstatement (INV-CEM-3a)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and has since been reinstated, and no other account uses ana.ruiz@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana.ruiz@example.org from My Account
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with ana.ruiz@example.org.
  • Closed account (INV-CEM-3)
    • Given: N1 is closed, with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: a change of N1's email to ana@example.org is requested
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • A request for someone else's account (INV-CEM-1)
    • Given: N1 and N2 are both active
    • When: a request from Ben asks to change N1's email
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only change your own email." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-CEM-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: a change of N9's email is requested
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on My Account. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. requester-mismatch (INV-CEM-1): who is asking is settled before anything else.
  2. neighbor-not-found (INV-CEM-10).
  3. email-missing (INV-CEM-11).
  4. The new email is the account's current one (INV-CEM-9): succeeds with nothing recorded.
  5. account-closed (INV-CEM-3).
  6. neighbor-suspended (INV-CEM-3a).
  7. email-in-use (INV-CEM-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
requester-mismatch You can only change your own email. INV-CEM-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CEM-10
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-CEM-11
account-closed This account is closed. INV-CEM-3
neighbor-suspended You can't change your email while your account is suspended. INV-CEM-3a
email-in-use That email address is already used by an account. INV-CEM-2

neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. email-missing, email-in-use, account-closed and neighbor-not-found mean the same conditions as in Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool, with the same sentences. email-in-use is one reason for every case of INV-CEM-2, so a refusal never reveals another account's status; its wording is the open question in Register Neighbor.

Idempotency: there is no request ID. A request whose effect has already happened, because the account's current email is already the one asked for, succeeds and records nothing (INV-CEM-9).

Requests at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Email Changed happen as one step, shared with Register Neighbor, so no two accounts are ever given the same email. Of two requests for the same email at once, from a sign-up or a change, at most one is recorded; the other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. Nothing is emailed when the email changes.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may change only their own email (INV-CEM-1); the shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Email Changed holds the neighbor's new email address. The old address stays in the earlier events as the shed's record; whether such details are kept for good is the retention question open in Register Neighbor.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time email check above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (this slice): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Registered matches slices/register-neighbor.md. The other three are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Account, Neighbors, Overdue Loans To Notify, Pickup Notices To Send, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the email). Register Neighbor and later Change Email requests check the new email as held.

Open Questions

  • How does the system know the request comes from the neighbor whose account it names? (brief 10 A1)
    • The same identity question is open in Add Tool, Register Neighbor and the neighbor screens.
    • Options: (a) callers say who they are, and nothing checks it; (b) a sign-in outside the model supplies the neighbor's ID; (c) sign-in is modeled as events and slices.
    • Recommendation: (b), which adds nothing to the model. If sign-in is by email, it must follow the account's current email after a change.
  • What makes a new email acceptable, and are two emails that differ only in capital letters the same? (brief 11 B3, B4)
    • These are the same open questions as at sign-up (Register Neighbor). Whatever is ruled there applies here too, with the same reason names.
    • Recommendation: as in Register Neighbor: a basic shape check, and compare without regard to case.
  • The wording of the email-in-use refusal (brief 11 B6).
  • Whether earlier email addresses are kept for good (brief 11 B7).
"},{"index":2,"name":"Suspend Neighbor","x0":458.76,"x1":602.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Suspend Neighbor

Intent

Let the shed manager suspend any active neighbor, so someone who keeps returning tools late stops borrowing until the shed manager reinstates them. Usually the neighbor has been flagged for late returns. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager issues Suspend Neighbor from either of two screens:

  • Flagged Neighbors, for a neighbor the system has flagged for late returns.
  • Neighbors, for any active neighbor, flagged or not. This covers a neighbor who closed their account while suspended and signed up again with a different email.

The Neighbors-screen trigger isn't drawn on the diagram; this doc is its specification. The system never suspends anyone: reaching the late-return threshold only flags a neighbor.

Command / Input

Command: Suspend Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor to suspend. Must be a registered account (INV-SUS-10) that isn't closed (INV-SUS-2).

There is no reason or note field: nothing is recorded about why. The flag and its late returns are usually the reason, and a suspension from the Neighbors screen needs none. The command carries no "from" status: a late copy of an older request counts as a new request.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Flagged Neighbors @Shed Manager, and screen Neighbors @Shed Manager (the second trigger is specified here, not drawn).

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Suspended → context Neighbors Read by: Suspended Neighbors (the neighbor appears), Flagged Neighbors (the neighbor's entry drops off), Neighbors and My Account (status suspended), and Neighbors To Flag (a suspended neighbor is never flagged). Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor read it to refuse a suspended neighbor.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
suspendedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. A later Neighbor Reinstated lifts the suspension; a later suspension records a new Neighbor Suspended.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Suspended feeds Suspended Neighbors, Flagged Neighbors, Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Suspension's effects are rules of the slices that refuse a suspended neighbor, each with its own reason the neighbor can see: a suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, including one set aside for them (INV-CHK-7, Check Out Tool), extend a loan (INV-EXT-7, Extend Loan), place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9, Place Hold) or change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email). They keep what they already have: their loans stay out and they can return them (INV-RET-7, Return Tool), and their holds keep their places and can be cancelled. A set-aside they can't collect expires at the end of its collect-by date, as any other (Expire Hold). While suspended they are never flagged (Flag Neighbor, INV-FLG-5). A suspension lasts until the shed manager reinstates the neighbor (Reinstate Neighbor); it never lifts by itself and is never permanent. The neighbor isn't emailed: they see the suspension on My Account and as the reason whenever something is refused. Flagged Neighbors, Suspended Neighbors, Neighbors and My Account own how a suspension is shown.

  • INV-SUS-1: Only the shed manager suspends a neighbor.
    • How the shed manager is recognised is the open identity question below.
  • INV-SUS-2: Only an active neighbor can be suspended.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed can't be suspended, because closed is final.
    • Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended changes nothing (INV-SUS-9).
  • INV-SUS-9: Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second suspension.
  • INV-SUS-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: suspending a flagged neighbor (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is active and on Flagged Neighbors after three late returns within 90 days. She has the ladder on loan and a hold waiting on the cordless drill.
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 from Flagged Neighbors
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded: her loan and her hold are untouched.
  • Suspending a neighbor who isn't flagged (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is active and not flagged
    • When: the shed manager suspends N2 from the Neighbors screen
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N2.
  • Suspending again after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and later reinstated, so she is active
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1
    • Then: a new Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1.
  • Already suspended (INV-SUS-9)
    • Given: N1 is suspended
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A late copy after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: the shed manager suspended N1, and then reinstated her
    • When: a delayed copy of the earlier Suspend Neighbor request for N1 arrives
    • Then: it counts as a new request: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1 again.
  • Closed account (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N3's account is closed
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N3
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Closed while suspended (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N4 was suspended and then closed their account
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N4
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." Its status is closed, not suspended, so this isn't treated as a repeat. No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-SUS-1)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: a request that doesn't come from the shed manager asks to suspend N1
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can suspend neighbors." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-SUS-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: the shed manager asks to suspend N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the screen they acted from. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-shed-manager (INV-SUS-1): who is asking is settled before anything else.
  2. neighbor-not-found (INV-SUS-10).
  3. If the neighbor's status is already suspended, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-SUS-9). Status is tested with closed first: an account closed while suspended has status closed, so it gets account-closed, not the repeat.
  4. account-closed (INV-SUS-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can suspend neighbors. INV-SUS-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-SUS-10
account-closed This account is closed. INV-SUS-2

not-shed-manager, neighbor-not-found and account-closed mean the same conditions as in Add Tool, Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool. neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screens, which offer Suspend only on listed neighbors. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: suspension is a state, and the command carries no "from" status. A request whose effect has already happened (the neighbor is suspended) succeeds and records nothing. A late copy of an older request that arrives after a reinstatement suspends again.

Requests at the same moment: Suspend Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A reinstatement or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may suspend a neighbor (INV-SUS-1). How the shed manager is recognised is the open identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Suspended links a neighbor to a suspension. It holds no name, email or reason.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (this slice): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Registered matches slices/register-neighbor.md. Reinstate Neighbor and Close Account are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Suspended Neighbors, Flagged Neighbors, Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag. Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor refuse a suspended neighbor; Reinstate Neighbor lifts the suspension.

Open Questions

  • Identity: how the system recognises the shed manager (brief 10 A1). This slice follows its answer; see the identity question in Add Tool.
"},{"index":3,"name":"Suspended Neighbors","x0":627.76,"x1":771.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Suspended Neighbors

Intent

Shows the shed manager every neighbor who is currently suspended, with when they were suspended, on the Suspended Neighbors screen they reinstate neighbors from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Suspended Neighbors screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per neighbor currently suspended, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Reinstate (Reinstate Neighbor slice), offered on every entry (INV-SPN-4).
  • A neighbor is suspended by the shed manager from Flagged Neighbors or from the Neighbors screen (Suspend Neighbor). No email goes to the neighbor on suspension or reinstatement, and no reason or note is recorded with a suspension.

Read Model / View

  • View: Suspended Neighbors built from events: "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Suspended Neighbors screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry appears or drops off shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Reinstate checks its own rules when it runs.

One row per suspended neighbor. A NeighborId is a UUID. An Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Neighbor Suspended.neighborId.
name Text Neighbor Registered.name for neighborId. Never changes.
email Text Neighbor Registered.email for neighborId, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email. Always the current one.
suspendedAt Instant Neighbor Suspended.suspendedAt. Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

To fill an entry when the suspension lands, the view also keeps every neighbor's name and current email. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned.

When an entry appears and drops off.

  • Neighbor Suspended creates the neighbor's entry.
  • Neighbor Reinstated removes it.
  • Neighbor Account Closed removes it.

Queries

  • List suspended neighbors. Takes nothing. Returns every entry with neighborId, name, email and suspendedAt. There is no paging. The order follows the shared list-order rule (open; see Open Questions).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-SPN-1: A neighbor appears on Suspended Neighbors when Neighbor Suspended is recorded for them, whether they were suspended from Flagged Neighbors or from the Neighbors screen.
  • INV-SPN-2: Each entry shows the neighbor's name and current email and the date they were suspended.
    • The name comes from Neighbor Registered. The email is the current one: Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it.
    • A suspended neighbor can't change their email. The email shown is the one they had when they were suspended, which may itself have been changed before; it changes again only after they are reinstated, by which time they have left the list.
    • No reason or note is recorded with a suspension, so none is shown.
  • INV-SPN-3: A suspended neighbor stays on the list until they are reinstated or close their account.
    • A suspension never lifts by itself after a set time, and it is never permanent.
  • INV-SPN-4: Every entry offers Reinstate, and a reinstated neighbor leaves the list.
    • Reinstating is the only action this screen offers.
  • INV-SPN-5: When a suspended neighbor closes their account, they leave the list.
    • Closed is final, so the shed manager is never offered Reinstate on a closed account.
  • INV-SPN-6: A neighbor appears on the list at most once.
    • A neighbor who is reinstated and later suspended again appears again, with the new date.
  • INV-SPN-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Only the shed manager sees Suspended Neighbors; neighbors never do. Only Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated and Neighbor Account Closed add or remove entries; Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed supply names and emails.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org, and Ben Ito with ben@example.org.

  • Neighbor suspended (INV-SPN-1, INV-SPN-2, INV-SPN-4)
    • Given: Suspended Neighbors is empty
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana on 7 October
    • Then: Suspended Neighbors lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, suspended 7 October, with Reinstate offered.
  • Email changed before suspension (INV-SPN-2)
    • Given: Ana changed her email to ana.ruiz@example.net before she was suspended
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Suspended Neighbors lists Ana Ruiz, ana.ruiz@example.net.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-SPN-4)
    • Given: Suspended Neighbors lists Ana and Ben
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana leaves Suspended Neighbors. Ben is still listed.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-SPN-5)
    • Given: Suspended Neighbors lists Ana
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana leaves Suspended Neighbors.
  • Suspended again after reinstatement (INV-SPN-6)
    • Given: Ana was suspended on 7 October and reinstated on 1 November
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana again on 3 February
    • Then: Suspended Neighbors lists Ana once, suspended 3 February.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-SPN-9)
    • Given: Suspended Neighbors lists Ana once
    • When: the same Neighbor Suspended for Ana is applied again
    • Then: Ana is still listed once, suspended 7 October.
  • Listing suspended neighbors
    • Given: Suspended Neighbors lists Ana and Ben
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists suspended neighbors
    • Then: both entries are returned with all their fields, with no paging.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-SPN-9).
  • Events after an entry is gone: once an entry has been removed, a later Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Account Closed for that neighbor changes nothing. A later Neighbor Suspended starts a new entry.
  • Stale actions: Reinstate offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, on a neighbor who has just closed their account). Reinstate Neighbor checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Suspended Neighbors screen is the shed manager's alone. How the system recognises the shed manager is the identity question (see Open Questions).
  • PII & compliance: shows suspended neighbors' names and current emails to the shed manager only. An entry is removed on reinstatement or account closure.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId, suspendedAt.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs and Suspend Neighbor's Neighbor Suspended {neighborId, suspendedAt}.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Reinstate Neighbor.

Open Questions

  • How a person is recognised (the identity question) — brief 10 A1.
  • List order — brief 10 A4.
  • How long personal data is kept — brief 11 B7. This screen shows neighbors' names and emails.
